text:
B: Hi! Can you hear me? Hello?
A: Yeah, yeah, I can hear you.
B: Oh good, sorry, the sound went funny for a second. I'm Gemma, I'm in Maidstone, in Kent.
A: Hardik. I'm in Kingsbury, north-west London.
B: Oh right, not too far then. So, erm, what do you do?
A: I work at a supermarket. Replenishment, so shelf-stacking, unloading deliveries. Part-time.
B: Oh okay. Is that by choice, the part-time, or...?
A: Sort of. It's school runs. It's me and my daughter, so I do nine-thirty till half two.
B: Ah, that makes sense. I'm a branch manager at a lettings and estate agency, so I've got a team of five, landlords, tenants, all the complaints come to me, basically. It's a lot. I had a landlord ring me at nine o'clock on a Sunday night last week, about a dripping tap. On a Sunday! Sorry, I'm going on already.
A: Nah, it's fine. Nine on a Sunday's a bit much.
B: It did my head in, honestly. How old's your daughter?
A: Six. Year 2.
B: Aw. Mine's twelve, Maisie, she's in Year 8. Twelve's a whole different thing, believe me. All she talks about is getting an iPhone because all her friends have got one. Does yours do that yet?
A: Not phones, no. She wants a hamster. I'm trying to hold out.
B: Ha, don't do it. We got a dog, a cockapoo, Biscuit, and he's eaten another sock this week. That's the third one. We've been to the vet before with it, I was convinced he was going to need an operation.
A: Erm, that's sort of why I'm saying no, to be honest. Can't really afford a vet.
B: No, fair enough. They're a fortune.
A: Yeah.
B: So, erm, did you do alright on the puzzle bit at the start?
A: It was alright. Some of them I got. The pattern one I kind of guessed.
B: I think I guessed half of them, to be honest. I'm better with people than puzzles. That's my job, really, reading people, spotting a problem tenant before they sign anything.
A: Yeah, I can imagine you'd need that.
B: You do. So is it just you looking after her then, full-time?
A: Mostly. She goes to her mum's in Leicester some weekends and holidays. My mum helps as well, she lives ten minutes away. She sends me back with way too much food every week, theplas, curries, everything.
B: Oh, that's nice though, isn't it? I wish my mum did that. She's just had her knee done, so it's the other way round at the moment, I'm sort of running round after her.
A: Sorry to hear that. Is she alright?
B: Yeah, she's getting there, thanks. It just makes you realise, you know? Anyway, do you get much time to yourself, with work and everything?
A: Not really. After she's in bed I play a bit of FIFA, watch the cricket highlights. India lost the last one, so that was a bad night, innit.
B: Oh no! I couldn't tell you a single cricket player, sorry. My husband's more into football. Do you ever get to...
